userStories.title: Scan root and mono nax configs for literal secrets
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add and export the single config-secret scanner and result types.

**Motivation** — The residual risk of opening reads is secret exposure: the config schema accepts literal values in `reporters.webhook.headers`, `reporters.otel.headers`, `agent.native.catalogOverrides[].headers`, `models.<agent>.<tier>.env` and `mcp.servers.<id>.env`, and anything the agent reads is sent to its model provider.

**Approach** — Scanner — `scanConfigSecrets(repoRoot)` reads the root config plus every mono config file and returns findings as `{ file, pointer, kind }`. It never returns a flagged value. Secret detection reuses nax-agent's existing, already-exported `redactSecrets` from `@nathapp/nax-agent/internal` (`packages/nax-agent/src/internal/redact.ts`). That function applies the key-name pattern when given an object (`redactSecrets({ [key]: value })`) and the value patterns (`sk-…`, GitHub, npm, AWS, Slack, PEM, JWT, `Bearer`/`Basic`, `url-credentials`, `TOKEN=…` assignments) when given a string. A value counts as flagged when the redacted result differs from the input. No pattern list is copied into nax.

Files scanned:
- `<repoRoot>/.nax/config.json`, when present.
- Every `config.json` under `<repoRoot>/.nax/mono/` with **at least one** directory segment between `mono/` and `config.json` — `.nax/mono/apps/api/config.json` and `.nax/mono/packages/app/config.json` are scanned; `.nax/mono/config.json` is not. This is the same set `isNaxConfigFile` accepts.

`files` is sorted lexicographically, and `findings` are grouped by file in that order, each file's in depth-first traversal order. A missing root config or a missing `mono/` directory is not a finding. When nothing is scanned, `files` is empty and `clean` is `true`.

A file that cannot be read, is not valid JSON, or whose top-level JSON value is not an object yields one finding, `{ file, pointer: "", kind: "unscannable" }`, and no other findings for that file. Scanning the remaining files continues.

Each parsed object is walked depth-first, through nested objects and arrays (array elements get their index as the pointer segment). Only string leaves are tested; numbers, booleans and `null` are ignored. Pointer segments are escaped per RFC 6901 (`~` → `~0`, `/` → `~1`), so a header key `X/Token` appears as `X~1Token`.

**Environment references.** `$VAR` and `${VAR}` (name `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`) are references. For each leaf, `stripped` is the value with every reference removed.

A string leaf yields **at most one finding**; the first rule that matches wins, in this fixed order:

1. **`literal-header`** — an ancestor key is `headers`, the leaf key (case-insensitive) is not one of `content-type`, `accept`, `user-agent`, `http-referer`, `x-title`, and the value contains no reference.
2. **`secret-env`** — an ancestor key is `env`, the value contains no reference, and `redactSecrets({ [leafKey]: value })[leafKey] !== value`. This flags a secret-looking key (`API_TOKEN`, `DATABASE_URL`) or a token-shaped value under any key, and leaves `NODE_ENV: "test"` alone.
3. **`token-shape`** — anywhere, `redactSecrets(stripped) !== stripped`.

So `"Bearer ${OPENROUTER_KEY}"` under `headers` is clean (it carries a reference and its stripped remainder `"Bearer "` is not token-shaped), while `"Bearer ${KEY} sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu"` is a `token-shape` finding.

**Scope** — In: scanner module, config barrel export and tests. Out: precheck/doctor (US-002), native read gate (US-003), prompt hint (US-004); no nax-agent edits or duplicate pattern lists.

**Interface**
```typescript
export type ConfigSecretKind = "literal-header" | "secret-env" | "token-shape" | "unscannable";
export interface ConfigSecretFinding {
  readonly file: string;     // repo-root-relative, posix: ".nax/config.json" | ".nax/mono/apps/api/config.json"
  readonly pointer: string;  // RFC 6901 JSON pointer to the flagged string; "" for "unscannable"
  readonly kind: ConfigSecretKind;
}
export interface ConfigSecretScan {
  readonly clean: boolean;                          // findings.length === 0
  readonly files: readonly string[];                // repo-root-relative paths actually scanned
  readonly findings: readonly ConfigSecretFinding[];
}
export async function scanConfigSecrets(repoRoot: string): Promise<ConfigSecretScan>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: scanConfigSecrets(root) resolves to { clean: true, files: [".nax/config.json"], findings: [] } when .nax/config.json is {} and no .nax/mono/ directory exists.
scanConfigSecrets(root) resolves to { clean: true, files: [], findings: [] } when root has no .nax/config.json.

scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { file: ".nax/config.json", pointer: "/reporters/webhook/headers/Authorization", kind: "literal-header" } and clean: false when that header holds the literal "Bearer abc12345xyz".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports no finding for a reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value of "Bearer ${OPENROUTER_KEY}".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports no finding for a reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value of "$OPENROUTER_KEY".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports no finding for a reporters.webhook.headers.HTTP-Referer value of "https://example.com".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { pointer: "/mcp/servers/github/env/GITHUB_TOKEN", kind: "secret-env" } when mcp.servers.github.env.GITHUB_TOKEN holds the literal "abc".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports no finding for models.native.fast.env.NODE_ENV holding "test".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports exactly one finding, of kind secret-env, for models.native.fast.env.NODE_ENV holding "sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports exactly one finding, of kind literal-header, for a reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value of "sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { pointer: "/quality/commands/test", kind: "token-shape" } when quality.commands.test is "DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@localhost/db bun test".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports no finding when quality.commands holds test: "bun run test" and testScoped: "bunx vitest run {{files}}".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports a finding with pointer /mcp/servers/x/args/1 and kind token-shape when mcp.servers.x.args is ["--token", "ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx"].
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports pointer /reporters/webhook/headers/X~1Token for a literal value under the header key X/Token.

scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { pointer: "/agent/native/catalogOverrides/0/headers/Authorization", kind: "literal-header" } when agent.native.catalogOverrides[0].headers.Authorization holds the literal "Bearer abc12345xyz".
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports a token-shape finding whose file is ".nax/mono/packages/app/config.json" when that mono file's quality.commands.test embeds postgres://u:p@localhost/db.
scanConfigSecrets(root) leaves .nax/mono/config.json out of files and reports clean: true when only that file embeds postgres://u:p@localhost/db.
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { file: ".nax/config.json", pointer: "", kind: "unscannable" } when .nax/config.json holds not json.
scanConfigSecrets(root) reports { file: ".nax/config.json", pointer: "", kind: "unscannable" } when .nax/config.json holds the JSON string "sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstu".
scanConfigSecrets(root) still reports the token-shape finding of a valid .nax/mono/apps/api/config.json when .nax/config.json holds not json.
The JSON serialisation of the ConfigSecretScan returned for the "Bearer abc12345xyz" header config omits the string abc12345xyz.

routing.reasoning: One new scanner module and one barrel export use established redaction patterns; strict test isolation is required because a false negative can expose credentials.

suggestedCriteria: scanConfigSecrets(root) reports one unscannable finding for an unreadable root config and still reports findings in readable mono configs.
scanConfigSecrets(root) returns lexicographically sorted files and file-grouped depth-first findings when root and multiple mono configs exist.

userStories.title: Surface config-secret warnings through precheck and doctor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Report the scanner as a non-blocking precheck warning and expose light precheck via `nax doctor`.

**Motivation** — Agents do want to read the file, to learn the package's declared commands. Two live runs on 2026-10-11 produced 5 refused config reads, all of them command lookups.

**Approach** — `runEnvironmentPrecheck` and `runPrecheck` also run `checkConfigSecrets(workdir)` **regardless of blockers**, after the blocker phase, filing the result under `passed` or `warnings` and printing it like any other check. `getEnvironmentWarnings` is unchanged. The added logic lives in a helper exported from `src/precheck/checks-config-secrets.ts`; the complexity baselines for `runEnvironmentPrecheck` and `runPrecheck` in `complexity-baseline.json` are not raised.

`nax doctor [-d <dir>] [--json]` is an alias for `nax precheck --light [-d <dir>] [--json]`: `doctorCommand` awaits `_doctorDeps.runTrustGate(dir)` and then `_doctorDeps.precheckCommand({ dir, json, light: true })`. Output (human and `--json`) and exit codes (`0` when no blocker fails, `1` when one does) are therefore those of `precheck --light`.

`config-secrets` is a Tier-2 warning that runs even when a blocker fails, so it is reported on a dirty or non-git working tree; a finding never changes the exit code. When the check fails, its `message` names each finding's `file`, `pointer` and `kind` and tells the user to move the value into an environment-variable reference or into the global `~/.nax/config.json` (which agents cannot reach). An invalid-JSON project config fails `loadConfig` before precheck runs, so through `nax doctor` it surfaces as a config-load error rather than an `unscannable` finding. The flagged value never appears in the output.

**Failure handling** — `_configSecretsCheckDeps.scanConfigSecrets` rejects inside `checkConfigSecrets`: returns `{ name: "config-secrets", tier: "warning", passed: false }` with a message saying the nax config could not be scanned; closed.

**Scope** — In: precheck integration and new doctor command including CLI and barrel exports. Out: scanner implementation (US-001), native read gate (US-003), prompt hint (US-004). Other `nax doctor` checks (git-tracked generated files, stale-artifact cleanup) — `nax doctor` runs exactly the `nax precheck --light` check set.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const _configSecretsCheckDeps: { scanConfigSecrets: typeof scanConfigSecrets };
export async function checkConfigSecrets(workdir: string): Promise<Check>; // name "config-secrets", tier "warning"
export const _doctorDeps: { runTrustGate: typeof runTrustGate; precheckCommand: typeof precheckCommand };
export async function doctorCommand(options: { dir: string; json?: boolean }): Promise<void>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: checkConfigSecrets(root) returns { name: "config-secrets", tier: "warning", passed: true } when root/.nax/config.json is {}.
checkConfigSecrets(root) returns passed: false with a message naming /reporters/webhook/headers/Authorization when that header holds the literal "Bearer abc12345xyz".
checkConfigSecrets(root) returns a message that omits abc12345xyz when reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization holds the literal "Bearer abc12345xyz".
checkConfigSecrets(root) returns passed: false with a message naming "could not scan" when _configSecretsCheckDeps.scanConfigSecrets rejects.

runEnvironmentPrecheck(config, root, { format: "json", silent: true }) resolves with a blockers entry and a warnings entry named config-secrets when root is a plain non-git directory whose .nax/config.json holds a literal reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value.

runPrecheck(config, prd, { workdir: root, format: "json", silent: true }) resolves with a result.warnings entry named config-secrets when root/.nax/config.json holds a literal reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value.
doctorCommand({ dir: "/repo", json: true }) awaits _doctorDeps.runTrustGate("/repo") before invoking _doctorDeps.precheckCommand.
doctorCommand({ dir: "/repo", json: true }) invokes _doctorDeps.precheckCommand once with { dir: "/repo", json: true, light: true }.

When running nax doctor --json -d <fixture>, where <fixture> is a plain non-git directory whose .nax/config.json holds a literal header value, then the JSON warnings include an entry named config-secrets.
When running nax doctor --json -d <fixture>, then it prints the same JSON payload as nax precheck --light --json -d <fixture> on the same fixture.

routing.reasoning: Security-sensitive reporting of credential findings across precheck orchestration, command trust gate and CLI without leaking values.

userStories.title: Gate native config reads while preserving all write refusals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wrap the owned-path policy and scan each native coding-tool dispatch before admitting path-named config reads.

**Motivation** — `isNaxConfigFile` refuses nax config files to **every** tool, reads included, through `resolveWithin` — the single containment seam in nax-agent. The reason the refusal states is a write concern: `quality.commands` and `acceptance.command` run through a shell without passing the permission gate, so a model that could edit the file could run an ungated command on the next run. Blocking writes is sufficient for that concern; blocking reads is collateral.

**Approach** — Read gate — `createConfigReadGatePolicy(base, configReadable)` wraps nax's existing `naxOwnedPathsPolicy` instead of editing `src/agents/nax-owned-writes.ts`. That file has a verbatim copy in `packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/nax-owned-paths.ts`, pinned by `test/unit/agents/nax-owned-writes-copy.test.ts`. A wrapper keeps both untouched, so no story crosses into `packages/nax-agent`.

`writeRefusal(tool, rel, …)` is called by nax-agent's `applyPathRules` for every path tool on the symlink-resolved `rel` (`packages/nax-agent/src/tools/policy.ts:169-171`). When reads are open, the wrapper refuses a nax config `rel` to every tool except an explicit read-only set (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `ScratchpadRead`, `ScratchpadList`). That covers `ScratchpadWrite` through a symlink, `Git` pathspecs (so committed config history is not readable), and any tool added later.

`resolveCodingToolSupport` opens reads only when Bash is either not declared for the dispatch or runs in `raw` approval mode, where the raw screen consults `bashRefusal`. A dispatch that declares Bash under `gated` or `escalate` keeps reads closed. `_codingToolSupportDeps` adds `scanConfigSecrets: typeof scanConfigSecrets`; `resolveCodingToolSupport(options)` awaits `_codingToolSupportDeps.scanConfigSecrets(options.codingToolRoot)` and passes `ownedPaths: createConfigReadGatePolicy(_codingToolSupportDeps.ownedPaths, readable)`, where `readable = scan.clean && (resolved.bashApproval === "raw" || !declaredWithProviders.includes("Bash"))`. When `options.codingToolRoot` is undefined no scan runs and `readable` is `false`; `readable` is also `false` when the scan rejects. The scan happens only on the path that reaches `buildCodingToolSupport`, so an early `return undefined` (no declared tools) does no scan.

`createConfigReadGatePolicy(base, configReadable)` returns a policy that keeps `base`'s `deniedEntries`, `rootWriteDenies`, `scratchpadEntry` and `writeOptIns` unchanged. For config rel: when readable, `configRefusal` returns `undefined`, `writeRefusal` returns `undefined` only for `NAX_CONFIG_READ_TOOLS`, and every other tool receives `"<rel>" ` plus `NAX_CONFIG_WRITE_REFUSAL`; otherwise `configRefusal` appends `NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX` (names `nax doctor`) to the base refusal and `writeRefusal` delegates. For other rels both hooks delegate. In raw Bash, `bashRefusal` returns `undefined` only when readable, `ctx.verb === "names"`, `ctx.sandboxWrapped` is true, at least one candidate is config and none is PRD/queue; otherwise it delegates. Redirects into config remain refused. `NAX_CONFIG_WRITE_REFUSAL` says the file is nax configuration that only `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob` may open and no tool may modify, and gives the `quality.commands` / `acceptance.command` ungated-shell reason. The OS sandbox keeps the unwrapped policy for write denies.

**Scope** — In: wrapper policy, coding-tool dispatch integration, revised owned-path regression fixtures. Out: scanner creation (US-001), precheck/doctor (US-002), prompt hint (US-004). Any write access to `.nax/config.json` or `.nax/mono/**/config.json` — `NAX_NEVER_OPT_IN`, the OS sandbox write denies and the raw-Bash redirect refusal are unchanged. Editing `src/agents/nax-owned-writes.ts` or its verbatim copy `packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/nax-owned-paths.ts` — the read gate wraps `naxOwnedPathsPolicy` instead. Any change to `packages/nax-agent` — the port, `resolveWithin`, `outOfRootReason`, `policy-bash.ts` and `redactSecrets` are consumed as they are. Reads of global `~/.nax/` files (global config, profiles, credentials) — they sit outside the containment root and stay unreachable.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const NAX_CONFIG_READ_TOOLS: ReadonlySet<string>; // Read, Grep, Glob, ScratchpadRead, ScratchpadList
export const NAX_CONFIG_WRITE_REFUSAL: string;
export const NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX: string;
export function createConfigReadGatePolicy(base: OwnedPathsPolicy, configReadable: boolean): OwnedPathsPolicy;
```
acceptanceCriteria: createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).configRefusal(root, join(root, ".nax", "config.json")) returns undefined.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, false).configRefusal(root, join(root, ".nax", "config.json")) returns NAX_CONFIG_REFUSAL followed by NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX, and the suffix names nax doctor.
createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, false).configRefusal(root, join(root, "src", "a.ts")) returns undefined.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).writeRefusal(tool, ".nax/mono/apps/api/config.json", { optIns: new Set() }) returns '".nax/mono/apps/api/config.json" ' + NAX_CONFIG_WRITE_REFUSAL for each tool in Write, Edit, Delete, GitCommit, Git, ScratchpadWrite.
createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).writeRefusal(tool, ".nax/config.json", { optIns: new Set() }) returns undefined for each tool in NAX_CONFIG_READ_TOOLS.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).writeRefusal("Write", ".nax/features/f/prd.json", { optIns: new Set() }) returns the same string as naxOwnedPathsPolicy.writeRefusal for those arguments.
createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).bashRefusal("Bash", ".nax/config.json", [configCandidate], { root, verb: "names", sandboxWrapped: true }) returns undefined.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).bashRefusal("Bash", ".nax/config.json", [configCandidate], { root, verb: "names", sandboxWrapped: false }) returns the same string as naxOwnedPathsPolicy.bashRefusal for those arguments.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).bashRefusal("Bash", ".nax/config.json", [configCandidate], { root, verb: "redirects into", sandboxWrapped: true }) returns the same string as naxOwnedPathsPolicy.bashRefusal for those arguments.

createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).bashRefusal("Bash", "x", [configCandidate, queueCandidate], { root, verb: "names", sandboxWrapped: true }) returns the same string as naxOwnedPathsPolicy.bashRefusal for those arguments.
createConfigReadGatePolicy(naxOwnedPathsPolicy, true).deniedEntries is the same array as naxOwnedPathsPolicy.deniedEntries.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with codingToolRoot set to a root whose .nax/config.json is {} and bashApproval "raw", support.runtime.callTool("Read", { path: ".nax/config.json" }) returns kind ok with content {}.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with a root whose .nax/config.json is {}, support.runtime.callTool("Write", { path: ".nax/config.json", content: "x" }) returns kind denied with a reason mentioning quality.commands, and the file still holds {}.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with declared tools including ScratchpadWrite and a root whose .nax/config.json is {}, support.runtime.callTool("ScratchpadWrite", { path: "config-link.json", content: "x" }) targeting a .nax/scratchpad/config-link.json symlink to .nax/config.json returns kind denied, and the file still holds {}.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with declared tools including Bash, bashApproval "gated" and a root whose .nax/config.json is {}, support.runtime.callTool("Read", { path: ".nax/config.json" }) returns kind denied with a reason naming nax doctor.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with bashApproval "gated" and a root whose .nax/config.json is {}, support.runtime.callTool("Bash", { command: "echo x > .nax/config.json" }) returns kind denied, and the file still holds {}.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with a root whose .nax/config.json holds a literal reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value, support.runtime.callTool("Read", { path: ".nax/config.json" }) returns kind denied with a reason naming nax doctor.

Through resolveCodingToolSupport with a root whose .nax/config.json is {} but whose .nax/mono/apps/api/config.json holds a literal header value, support.runtime.callTool("Read", { path: ".nax/config.json" }) returns kind denied.
When resolveCodingToolSupport receives codingToolRoot: root and declaredTools: ["Read"] along with an unrestricted config, it invokes _codingToolSupportDeps.scanConfigSecrets once with root.
When _codingToolSupportDeps.scanConfigSecrets rejects, resolveCodingToolSupport resolves, and support.runtime.callTool("Read", { path: ".nax/config.json" }) returns kind denied.

routing.reasoning: A new owned-paths wrapper and dispatch integration span canonicalized path tools and Bash modes; strict test isolation is required for this access-control boundary.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test "Read of nax config is refused like a write" (line 91) asserts that Read of the root nax config is denied with CONFIG_REASON. Its fixture writes an empty JSON object to the root nax config, which the scan reports clean, so under US-003 that Read succeeds against a correct implementation. US-003 owns rewriting the test: with a fixture config holding a literal reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value, the Read is denied with a reason that starts with CONFIG_REASON and ends with NAX_CONFIG_READ_DISABLED_SUFFIX. ALSO: the test "Glob does not list nax config" (line 110) asserts that the naxcfg.json symlink to the root nax config yields "no matches". With the clean empty-object fixture, resolveWithin now admits the symlink target and Glob lists it. US-003 owns moving the "no matches" assertion onto a fixture whose root nax config holds a literal header value. ALSO: the test "Exec refuses a positional path to nax config" (line 125) asserts that RunCommand with argv bun add ./.nax/config.json errors with "resolves outside the permitted root". With the clean empty-object fixture the positional path is now admitted. US-003 owns moving that assertion onto a fixture whose root nax config holds a literal header value, where the error text is unchanged.

userStories.title: Hint at readable project commands in TDD prompts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Append a config-read hint only for prompts built against a clean, existing repo-root config.

**Motivation** — Agents do want to read the file, to learn the package's declared commands. Two live runs on 2026-10-11 produced 5 refused config reads, all of them command lookups — each costs a turn and ends in a guess.

**Approach** — Prompt hint — one paragraph appended by `buildNaxArtifactsSection` when an options flag is set; `TddPromptBuilder` sets it from a scan of the **repo root** it is handed through a new `configRoot(dir)` builder method (not the loader workdir, which is the package directory for a monorepo package story — `src/pipeline/types.ts:88-95`).

`buildNaxArtifactsSection(role, variant?, isolation?, options?: { configReadable?: boolean })`: With `options` omitted or `configReadable` not `true`, it returns exactly the baseline text. With `configReadable: true`, `buildNaxArtifactsSection` appends this paragraph after its last paragraph:

The project's declared commands (test, testScoped, lint, typecheck, build, ...) are in
`.nax/config.json` under `quality.commands`. In a monorepo, `.nax/mono/<package>/config.json`
overrides them per key for that package: a key set there wins, every other key comes from the
root file. Read them with the `Read` tool. Do not modify either file; nax config cannot be changed
from inside a run.

The per-key wording matches `quality.commands` deep-merge semantics (`src/config/merge.ts:61`). The hint keys off the scan alone, not the dispatch's Bash mode; in a `gated`/`escalate` Bash session the `Read` it points to is refused with the read-disabled reason.

`TddPromptBuilder.configRoot(dir: string): this`: When it was called, `build()` awaits `_tddPromptBuilderDeps.scanConfigSecrets(dir)` and passes `{ configReadable: scan.clean && scan.files.includes(".nax/config.json") }`; when it was not, no scan runs and no options are passed. The scan and its error handling live in a private helper; the `TddPromptBuilder.build` complexity baseline is not raised. `TddPromptBuilder.buildForRole(role, workdir, config, story, opts)` also chains `configRoot(opts.root)` when `opts.root` is defined (documented as the repo root where `.nax/` lives). Both builder chains in `promptStage.execute(ctx)` chain `configRoot(ctx.projectDir)`. If `_tddPromptBuilderDeps.scanConfigSecrets` rejects inside `build()`, the hint is omitted; `build()` resolves normally (closed).

**Scope** — In: artifacts section, TDD builder, single/batch pipeline prompt chains and associated tests. Out: scanner creation (US-001), precheck/doctor (US-002), policy gate (US-003). The rectifier prompt path (`src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder-helpers.ts`, `CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH`) and the `nax prompts` export CLI (`src/cli/prompts-tdd.ts`, `src/cli/prompts-export.ts`) — they do not call `configRoot`, so they keep the current `.nax/` artifacts text; rectifier sessions are still covered by the read gate.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function buildNaxArtifactsSection(role: GuardrailRole, variant?: "standard" | "lite", isolation?: "strict" | "lite", options?: { configReadable?: boolean }): string;
class TddPromptBuilder { configRoot(dir: string): this; }
export const _tddPromptBuilderDeps: { scanConfigSecrets: typeof scanConfigSecrets };
```
acceptanceCriteria: buildNaxArtifactsSection("implementer", undefined, undefined, { configReadable: true }) returns text that includes .nax/mono/<package>/config.json and quality.commands.
buildNaxArtifactsSection("implementer") returns the same string as buildNaxArtifactsSection("implementer", undefined, undefined, { configReadable: false }), and that string omits quality.commands.

PromptBuilder.for("tdd-simple").withLoader(join(root, "packages", "app"), config).configRoot(root).story(story).build() resolves to a prompt that includes .nax/mono/<package>/config.json when root/.nax/config.json is {}.

PromptBuilder.for("tdd-simple").withLoader(root, config).configRoot(root).story(story).build() resolves to a prompt that omits .nax/mono/<package>/config.json when root/.nax/config.json holds a literal reporters.webhook.headers.Authorization value.
PromptBuilder.for("tdd-simple").withLoader(root, config).configRoot(root).story(story).build() resolves to a prompt that omits .nax/mono/<package>/config.json when root has no .nax/config.json.

PromptBuilder.for("tdd-simple").withLoader(root, config).story(story).build() resolves to a prompt that omits .nax/mono/<package>/config.json, without invoking _tddPromptBuilderDeps.scanConfigSecrets, when configRoot is not called and root/.nax/config.json is {}.

outOfScope: Any write access to `.nax/config.json` or `.nax/mono/**/config.json` — `NAX_NEVER_OPT_IN`, the OS sandbox write denies and the raw-Bash redirect refusal are unchanged.
Editing `src/agents/nax-owned-writes.ts` or its verbatim copy `packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/nax-owned-paths.ts` — the read gate wraps `naxOwnedPathsPolicy` instead.
Any change to `packages/nax-agent` — the port, `resolveWithin`, `outOfRootReason`, `policy-bash.ts` and `redactSecrets` are consumed as they are.
Reads of global `~/.nax/` files (global config, profiles, credentials) — they sit outside the containment root and stay unreachable.
ACP agent sessions (Claude, Codex adapters) — they do not use the native coding-tool policy.
Redacting or masking secrets inside the Read result — a config with any finding is refused to `Read`, `Glob` and path-naming tools as a whole.

Content searches that do not name a config file — `Grep` over a directory such as `.nax`, `.nax/mono` or the repo root (its `rg` / `grep -r` child reads every file beneath without a per-file `resolveWithin` check), and raw Bash that builds a config path dynamically (for example `python3 -c` opening it) — can read config contents whatever the scan result. This residual exists today and is accepted; the gate covers tools and commands that name a config path.

A user-configurable allow-list for scanner false positives — the remedy is moving the value into an environment-variable reference (`reporters.*.headers` expand `${VAR}`), into the global `~/.nax/config.json`, or renaming it.

False positives inherited from the shared `redactSecrets` value patterns, such as an `sk-` run inside a longer command word (`test:task-runner-integration-suite`) — accepted; `nax doctor` names the pointer so the user can rename it.
A generic high-entropy detector — only the existing `redactSecrets` key and value patterns are used.

Scanning committed git history for secrets — the `Git` tool is refused explicit nax config `paths`/`refs` by the read gate, and pathless diff/log/show already exclude `.nax` (`NAX_OWNED_GIT_EXCLUDE_PATHSPECS`).

The rectifier prompt path (`src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder-helpers.ts`, `CONTRADICTION_ESCAPE_HATCH`) and the `nax prompts` export CLI (`src/cli/prompts-tdd.ts`, `src/cli/prompts-export.ts`) — they do not call `configRoot`, so they keep the current `.nax/` artifacts text; rectifier sessions are still covered by the read gate.
Other `nax doctor` checks (git-tracked generated files, stale-artifact cleanup) — `nax doctor` runs exactly the `nax precheck --light` check set.

US-003 only: whether Exec (`RunCommand` with `argv`) admits a positional `./.nax/config.json` under a clean scan is not pinned — Exec positional paths are checked through `resolveWithin` only and Exec runs package managers, while writes stay blocked by the OS sandbox and the write refusal.
US-003 only: an undefined `codingToolRoot` keeps the existing `CODING_TOOL_ROOT_MISSING` behaviour; the read gate adds nothing on that path.
US-003 only: the sandbox launcher (`resolveDispatchLauncher`) keeps receiving the unwrapped `naxOwnedPathsPolicy`, so the OS-level write denies are unchanged.
US-003 only: config edits made by a human mid-run are honoured at the next dispatch, because the scan runs per `resolveCodingToolSupport` call; no run-level caching is added.
